newsitem.title: USA: Prime says hotel closure won't hurt earnings.
newsitem.headline: Prime says hotel closure won't hurt earnings.

text.p: Prime Hospitality Corp said Tuesday it does not expect the temporary closure of its Marriott's Frenchman's Reef hotel in St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands, to have a material impact on earnings or cash flow due to the seasonality of the hotel's operations and the company's business interruption insurance coverage.
Prime closed the hotel in April for redevelopment, and plans to open it in December, it said.
The company said it is optimistic about its prospects to continue achieving high rates of growth in the second half of the year.
The company reported second quarter operating earnings per share, on a diluted basis, of $0.26, compared with earnings per share of $0.20 in the prior year period.

In a statement, Chairman and Chief Executive David Simon said, "As we build critical mass in our AmeriSuites chain, we expect to achieve greater visibility and name recognition. In addition, our recent Wellesley reimaging program has resulted in improved product quality and positions the chain for strong growth."
